item.name: Codex of the Last Archivist
entries: This black, leather-like spellbook is bound in tarnished silver and sealed by an eye-shaped clasp. Its pages appear blank until touched by its attuned keeper, whereupon silver script emerges across them. No reliable record identifies its maker or origin.

entries.name: Arcane Supremacy
entries: While holding the codex, you gain a +3 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your spells. The codex can be used as a Spellcasting Focus.

entries.name: Endless Archive
entries: The codex can be used as a spellbook and can contain any number of Wizard spells.
The time and gold required to copy a Wizard spell into the codex are halved.

When you finish a Long Rest, choose one Wizard spell recorded in the codex. That spell is always prepared for you until you finish your next Long Rest, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare.

entries.name: Forbidden Index
entries: You have Advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) checks concerning spells, magical writing, curses, artifacts, or lost magic.
{@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} and {@spell Identify|XPHB} are always prepared for you while you are attuned to the codex, and they don't count against the number of spells you can prepare.
You can also cast {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} and {@spell Identify|XPHB} from the codex without expending a spell slot.

entries.name: Archive the Unwritten
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet casts a spell of level 1 through 9, you can take a Reaction to record an echo of that spell in the codex as an Archived Spell.

Before you finish your next Long Rest, you can cast the Archived Spell once without expending a spell slot and without providing any Material components, regardless of their cost or whether they would normally be consumed. You use your own spellcasting ability for the spell.
Once you successfully archive a spell with this property, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Perfect Recollection
entries: When you cast a spell recorded in the codex using a spell slot, choose one of the following benefits:

items: You have Advantage on one spell attack roll made as part of the spell.
One creature affected by the spell has Disadvantage on the first saving throw it makes against the spell.
The spell ignores Resistance to one damage type it deals.

entries: You can use this property a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Unbroken Formula
entries: You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws made to maintain Concentration.
When you fail a Constitution saving throw to maintain Concentration, you can choose to succeed instead. Once you do so, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Final Annotation
entries: When you fail a saving throw against a spell or magical effect, you can choose to succeed instead. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Unblemished Archive
entries: The codex can't be permanently damaged or destroyed by ordinary means. Torn pages restore themselves, erased writing returns, and damage to its binding repairs itself.

If the codex is destroyed while it has a Soul-Bound keeper, it reforms beside that keeper at the next dawn with all of its recorded contents intact. If it has no Soul-Bound keeper, it reforms at the site where it was destroyed.

entries.name: Curse: The Endless Archive
entries: The codex bears a 9th-level curse. Attuning to it binds the keeper to the Archive.

entries.name: Soul Bound
entries: You can't willingly end your Attunement to the codex, willingly relinquish it, or willingly remain separated from it.
The codex can't be permanently taken from you by force. If it is separated from you, it reappears on your person after the separation can no longer be maintained.
No other creature can attune to the codex while your Soul Bound connection remains.

entries.name: Archivist's Claim
entries: While Soul Bound to the codex, you can't willingly attune to another cursed magic item.
You have Advantage on saving throws and ability checks made to resist an effect that would forcibly bind you to, possess you through, or establish magical ownership over you.

entries.name: Curse Suppression
entries: While the codex is in your possession, curse effects of 9th level or lower can't affect you. A curse originating from a magic item of Legendary rarity or lower is likewise suppressed against you.
A curse already affecting you is suppressed rather than removed while this property applies.
Artifacts, deities, and effects of comparable power can ignore this protection at the GM's discretion.

entries.name: Archive Remembers
entries: Arcane writing recorded in the codex can't be permanently erased, removed, or destroyed. Lost arcane writing returns the next time the codex is opened.

entries.name: Breaking the Curse
entries: {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} suppresses the Soul Bound curse and its restrictions for 24 hours but doesn't permanently end it.
{@spell Wish|XPHB} or magic of comparable power can permanently break the curse.

item.name: Ascendant Script Tattoo
entries: This tattoo resembles a line of arcane notation written directly into the skin. The symbols subtly rearrange themselves whenever their bearer casts a spell.

entries.name: Ascendant Casting
entries: When you cast a spell of level 1 through 8 using a spell slot, you can expend charges to treat the spell as though it were cast using a spell slot one level higher for each charge expended, to a maximum effective spell level of 9. You can expend no more than 2 charges on a single spell.

entries.name: Overflowing Spell
entries: When you use Ascendant Casting, you can expend 1 additional charge and choose one of the following effects:

items: {@b Empowered.} Reroll a number of the spell's damage dice up to your Proficiency Bonus. You must use the new rolls.
{@b Extended.} If the spell has a duration of at least 1 minute and isn't Instantaneous, double its duration, to a maximum of 24 hours.
{@b Far-Reaching.} If the spell has a range of at least 10 feet, double its range. If its range is Touch, its range becomes 30 feet.
{@b Overwhelming.} One creature affected by the spell has Disadvantage on the first saving throw it makes against the spell.

entries.name: Restored Script
entries: The tattoo regains {@dice 1d4 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn.

item.name: Mantle of the Unbroken Spell
entries: Arcane notation drifts across this dark mantle like ink beneath water. No maker's mark has ever been found on it.

entries.name: Unbroken Concentration
entries: You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws made to maintain Concentration.

entries.name: Spell Refuses to Break
entries: When you fail a Constitution saving throw to maintain Concentration, you can choose to succeed instead. You can use this property twice, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Arcane Stability
entries: When you take damage while concentrating on a spell, you can reduce the DC of the resulting Constitution saving throw by 5, to a minimum DC of 10.
You can use this property a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Persistent Spell
entries: If you become Incapacitated while concentrating on a spell, your Concentration doesn't immediately end. It ends at the end of your next turn unless you are no longer Incapacitated before then.
This property can't prevent death from ending your Concentration.

item.name: Earring of the Silent Word
entries: This single black earring bears one arcane glyph that has resisted every attempt at translation. Its origin is unknown.

entries.name: Silent Casting
entries: While wearing the earring, you can cast any spell that has a Verbal component without providing that Verbal component. Any Somatic or Material components are still required.

entries.name: Unspoken Word
entries: A spell cast without its Verbal component through this item produces no spoken incantation or sound from that component. A creature can't detect the casting solely by hearing speech, though this property doesn't conceal other components, visible manifestations, or sounds produced by the spell itself.

item.name: Coin of the Open Rite
entries: This old silver coin bears an incomplete magical circle resembling an open doorway. No known mint claims its design.

entries.name: Open Rite
entries: You can cast a prepared spell of level 1 through 3 as a Ritual even if the spell doesn't have the Ritual tag. The spell's normal casting time must be 1 minute or less.

Casting a spell this way increases its casting time by 10 minutes and doesn't expend a spell slot. You must still provide the spell's normal components, and its range, duration, Concentration, and other effects are unchanged.

item.name: Greater Coin of the Open Rite
entries: The circle engraved on this silver coin is nearly complete, except for a narrow break at its center.

entries.name: Greater Open Rite
entries: You can cast a spell of level 1 through 5 as a Ritual even if the spell doesn't have the Ritual tag. The spell must be known by you, prepared by you, or recorded in a spellbook or similar spellcasting source available to you, and its normal casting time must be 1 minute or less.

Casting a spell this way increases its casting time by 10 minutes and doesn't expend a spell slot. A spell recorded in a spellbook or similar source doesn't need to be prepared for you to cast it this way.
You must still provide the spell's normal components, and its range, duration, Concentration, and other effects are unchanged.

item.name: Grand Coin of the Open Rite
entries: The engraved circle on this coin appears complete until viewed closely, when a hairline opening becomes visible along its edge.

entries.name: Grand Open Rite
entries: You can cast a spell of level 1 through 7 as a Ritual even if the spell doesn't have the Ritual tag. The spell must be known by you, prepared by you, or recorded in a spellbook or similar spellcasting source available to you, and its normal casting time must be 1 minute or less.
Casting a spell this way increases its casting time by 10 minutes and doesn't expend a spell slot. You must be capable of casting spells of the chosen spell's level.

entries.name: Open Beyond Preparation
entries: You can cast an eligible spell directly from a spellbook or similar spellcasting source available to you even if the spell isn't prepared.

entries.name: Patient Invocation
entries: When using this coin, you can increase the additional casting time from 10 minutes to 1 hour. If you do, you don't need to provide Material components that aren't consumed and have a listed cost of 1,000 GP or less.
Consumed Material components and non-consumed components worth more than 1,000 GP are still required.

item.name: Final Coin of the Open Rite
entries: No visible break exists in the circle engraved upon this coin, yet its design still gives the unmistakable impression of an open door.

entries.name: Final Open Rite
entries: You can cast a spell of level 1 through 9 as a Ritual even if the spell doesn't have the Ritual tag. The spell must be known by you, prepared by you, or recorded in a spellbook or similar spellcasting source available to you, and its normal casting time must be 1 minute or less.
Casting a spell this way increases its casting time by 10 minutes and doesn't expend a spell slot. You must be capable of casting spells of the chosen spell's level.

entries.name: Ninth Door
entries: An eligible spell recorded in a spellbook or similar spellcasting source can be cast through the coin even if the spell isn't on your class's spell list. You use your own spellcasting ability for the spell.

entries.name: Perfect Invocation
entries: When using this coin, you can increase the additional casting time from 10 minutes to 1 hour. If you do, you don't need to provide Material components with a listed cost if those components aren't consumed by the spell.
Consumed Material components are still required.

entries.name: Sacrifice of Time
entries: Instead of the normal additional casting time, you can perform the rite over 8 hours. If you do, the coin can replace consumed Material components with a combined listed value of 10,000 GP or less. Components replaced in this way are considered consumed.

entries.name: Unbroken Rite
entries: If a ritual performed with this coin is interrupted, its progress remains intact for 1 hour. If you resume the same ritual during that time, you continue from the point at which it was interrupted rather than beginning again.
The coin can preserve only one unfinished ritual at a time.

race.name: Runeblood
entries: Runeblood are humanoids marked by living arcane inscriptions that form naturally across their bodies.
The markings differ greatly between individuals. Some appear as faint lines beneath the skin, others glow across the eyes or limbs, and some remain invisible until magic is used.
No reliable history explains where the inscriptions originate. Identical symbols have occasionally appeared on Runeblood separated by centuries and with no known relation to one another.

entries.name: Arcane Sight
entries: You can cast {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} without expending a spell slot.
Once you cast it with this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast it using any spell slots you have.

entries.name: Living Rune
entries: Choose one of the following runes when you select this species. Your choice is permanent.

items: {@b Aegis Rune.} When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce that damage by {@dice 1d8} + your Proficiency Bonus.
{@b Force Rune.} Once on each of your turns when you damage a creature with an attack or spell, you can deal an additional {@damage 1d8} Force damage to one creature damaged by it.
{@b Passage Rune.} As a Bonus Action, you teleport up to 20 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
{@b Insight Rune.} When you fail an ability check, you can roll {@dice 1d6} and add it to the check, potentially turning the failure into a success.

entries: You can activate your Living Rune a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Runic Magic
entries: You know the {@spell Prestidigitation|XPHB} cantrip.
Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your spellcasting ability for it.

entries.name: Read the Script
entries: You have Advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) checks made to understand magical runes, glyphs, inscriptions, or written magical effects.

entries.name: Runic Memory
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Arcana} skill. If you already have proficiency in Arcana, you instead gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill History}, {@skill Investigation}, or {@skill Religion}.

entries.name: Inscribed Focus
entries: You can use the runes on your body as a Spellcasting Focus for your spells.

race.name: Fragmentborn
entries: Fragmentborn are humanoids carrying an unknown fragment within their body, mind, or soul.
A fragment may appear as crystal beneath the skin, an unusual scar, a symbol suspended within an eye, a faint distortion around the body, or nothing visible at all.

Fragments don't appear to share a single origin. Attempts to remove or identify them have produced inconsistent results, and in many cases the fragment seems to exist in a form that can't be physically isolated.

entries.name: Fragment Sense
entries: You can cast {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} without expending a spell slot.
Once you cast it with this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Fragment Nature
entries: Choose one of the following manifestations when you select this species. Your choice is permanent.

items: {@b Aegis Fragment.} When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce the damage by {@dice 1d8} + your Proficiency Bonus.
{@b Arcane Fragment.} Choose one cantrip from the Wizard spell list. You know that cantrip. Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your spellcasting ability for it.
{@b Echo Fragment.} When you fail an ability check or saving throw, you can roll {@dice 1d4} and add it to the roll, potentially turning the failure into a success.
{@b Rift Fragment.} As a Bonus Action, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
{@b Void Fragment.} Once on each of your turns when you damage a creature with an attack or spell, you can deal an additional {@damage 1d6} Force damage to one creature damaged by it.

entries: If your Fragment Nature has an activated effect, you can use that effect a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Fragment Stability
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws against effects that would alter your form against your will.

entries.name: Uncertain Presence
entries: Magic that determines your exact nature, origin, or supernatural identity can reveal that you carry an unusual magical presence, but it doesn't automatically reveal the nature or origin of your fragment.

entries.name: Fragment Resonance
entries: You have Advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) checks made to identify portals, teleportation effects, magical anomalies, or effects that alter space or reality.

entries.name: Anchored Form
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws and ability checks made to resist being teleported or moved against your will by a magical effect.

race.name: Spellforged
entries: Spellforged are living Constructs built around an internal magical structure known as a Spellcore.
Their bodies vary greatly in material and design. Metal, stone, crystal, porcelain, wood, and stranger substances have all been documented.
No surviving record identifies an original creator, and Spellforged discovered in completely unrelated locations sometimes contain identical internal components.

entries.name: Constructed Existence
entries: You don't need to eat, drink, breathe, or sleep.
Magic can't put you to sleep.
You must still complete a Long Rest to gain its benefits. During a Long Rest, you spend at least 6 hours in an inactive state, during which you remain conscious and can see and hear normally.

entries.name: Arcane Chassis
entries: While you aren't wearing armor, your base Armor Class is 13 + your Dexterity modifier.
You can use a Shield and still gain this benefit.

entries.name: Integrated Spell Focus
entries: Your body can function as a Spellcasting Focus for any spell you cast that allows the use of a Spellcasting Focus.

entries.name: Arcane Maintenance
entries: When {@spell Mending|XPHB} is cast on you, you can expend one Hit Point Die and roll it. You regain Hit Points equal to the number rolled + your Constitution modifier.
Once you regain Hit Points this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

entries.name: Spellcore Configuration
entries: Choose one of the following configurations when you select this species. Your choice is permanent.

items: {@b Aegis Core.} When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce the damage by {@dice 1d8} + your Proficiency Bonus.
{@b Arcane Core.} Choose one cantrip from the Wizard spell list. You know that cantrip. Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your spellcasting ability for it.
{@b Assault Core.} Once on each of your turns when you damage a creature with an attack or spell, you can deal an additional {@damage 1d6} Force damage to one creature damaged by it.
{@b Mobility Core.} As a Bonus Action, you teleport up to 20 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
{@b Restoration Core.} As a Bonus Action, you or one creature you touch regains {@dice 1d6} + your Proficiency Bonus Hit Points.

entries: If your Spellcore Configuration has an activated effect, you can use that effect a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Construct Resilience
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Poisoned condition.
You also have Resistance to Poison damage.

entries.name: Integrated Compartment
entries: Your body contains a small concealed compartment. It can hold objects with a combined weight of up to 5 pounds, provided each object can fit within a space roughly 1 foot on a side.
Finding the compartment while it is closed requires a successful Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check against a DC equal to 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Constitution modifier.
Opening or closing the compartment requires the Utilize action.

race.name: Arcane Aberrant
entries: Arcane Aberrants are humanoids whose bodies have been permanently altered by magical forces.

The changes vary enormously between individuals. One may possess unusually colored blood, crystalline growths beneath the skin, shifting patterns across the eyes, or faint magical distortions surrounding their body. Others appear almost entirely ordinary until their magic begins to surface.

Whether these alterations are inherited, caused by exposure to powerful magic, or originate from something far older remains uncertain. What is known is that the magic within an Arcane Aberrant never remains completely still. Their bodies continue to adapt around it throughout their lives.

entries.name: Age
entries: Arcane Aberrants reach adulthood at roughly the same rate as Humans. Their maximum lifespan is unknown, and no Arcane Aberrant has yet been confirmed to die from old age.

entries.name: Natural Inclination
entries: Increase your Ability Scores by a total of {@b 2 points}.
These increases are separate from those granted by your Background.

entries.name: Gradual Development
entries: When you select this species, choose one Ability Score as your {@b Primary Ability} and a different Ability Score as your {@b Secondary Ability}. These choices are permanent.
At character levels {@b 5, 9, 13, and 17}, your Primary Ability increases by {@b 1}.
Your Secondary Ability further strengthens your Primary Ability. For every {@b 2 points} your Secondary Ability has above 10, your Primary Ability increases by {@b 1}.
If your Secondary Ability increases or decreases enough to cross one of these thresholds, the increase granted to your Primary Ability changes accordingly.
Increases granted by this trait are separate from Ability Score increases granted by your Background, Feats, or other features.

entries.name: Mutative Instinct
entries: When you fail an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can roll {@dice 1d4} and add it to the roll, potentially turning the failure into a success.
You can use this trait a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
The die becomes {@dice 1d6} when your Proficiency Bonus becomes +4, {@dice 1d8} when it becomes +5, and {@dice 1d10} when it becomes +6.

entries.name: Aberrant Magic
entries: Magic has become an intrinsic part of your body.
You know the {@spell Prestidigitation|XPHB} cantrip.
Starting at character level 3, you can cast {@spell Chromatic Orb|XPHB} once without expending a spell slot or providing its Material component.
Starting at character level 5, you can cast {@spell Alter Self|XPHB} once without expending a spell slot.
You regain the ability to cast each of these spells with this trait when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast them using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your spellcasting ability for these spells.
Your body can serve as a Spellcasting Focus for your spells.

entries.name: Resilient Metabolism
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Poisoned condition.
You also have Resistance to Poison damage.

entries.name: Heightened Senses
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Perception} skill.
You also have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.

feat.name: Spell Thief
entries: You have learned to seize the lingering structure of another creature's magic before it fades.

entries.name: Steal Spell
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet casts a spell of level 1 or higher, you can take a Reaction to attempt to steal an echo of that spell.
The spell must be of a level no higher than your Proficiency Bonus and no higher than 5th level.
Make an ability check using your spellcasting ability. The DC equals 10 + the spell's level. On a success, you store the spell within yourself.
You can have only one stolen spell at a time. Stealing another spell causes the previous one to be lost.

entries.name: Stolen Casting
entries: While you have a stolen spell, you can cast it once without expending a spell slot, using the same level at which you stole it.
The stolen spell counts as one of your spells while you hold it, and you use your own spellcasting ability for its attack rolls and saving throw DC.
You must provide any Material components the spell normally requires, including components that have a cost or are consumed.
After you cast the stolen spell, it disappears from you.
If unused, the stolen spell disappears when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Arcane Larceny
entries: Once you successfully steal a spell, you can't successfully steal another spell until you finish a Long Rest.

feat.name: Arcane Reflex
entries: You have developed an instinctive response to creatures using magic around you.

entries.name: Arcane Reflex
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet casts a spell, you can use your Reaction to move up to half your Speed.
Immediately after this movement, you can do one of the following against that creature:

items: Make one attack with a weapon.
Cast a cantrip that has a casting time of an Action and makes an attack roll.

entries: This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

entries.name: Spell Resistance
entries: When you succeed on a saving throw against a spell, you take no damage and suffer no other effect from that spell that would normally occur on a successful save.

feat.name: Spellcrafting
entries: You have learned to dismantle and reconstruct the structure of spells.

entries.name: Spellcrafting
entries: When you cast a spell using a spell slot, you can choose a different spell you know or have prepared and expend a spell slot capable of casting that spell as well.
Choose any number of the following properties from the second spell and replace the corresponding properties of the spell you are casting:

items: {@b Range.}
{@b Duration.}
{@b Damage Dice and Damage Type.}
{@b Saving Throw.}
{@b Spell Attack.}
{@b Area of Effect.}
{@b Spell Effect.}

entries: You can replace one, several, or all of these properties.
Any part you don't replace remains unchanged from the original spell.

entries.name: Spellcrafting Uses
entries: You can use Spellcrafting a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier, with a minimum of once.
You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: The Archive
entries: Some wizards fill spellbooks. Others preserve discoveries, theories, and fragments of forgotten lore. You possess something fundamentally different.

You gain the Pact of the Tome Eldritch Invocation without needing to meet its prerequisites. This invocation doesn't count against the number of Eldritch Invocations granted by Forbidden Invocations. The Book of Shadows created by Pact of the Tome becomes your Archive and also functions as your Wizard spellbook.

entries.name: Endless Pages
entries: The Archive possesses effectively endless pages. It can contain any number of Wizard spells, Pact magic, magical formulae, research, maps, drawings, notes, history, diagrams, and other written or illustrated information.
Whenever one of your features refers to your spellbook or your Book of Shadows, the Archive qualifies as both.

entries.name: Expanded Tome
entries: Whenever Pact of the Tome allows you to select spells or cantrips for your Book of Shadows, you can select them from any spell list. You use Intelligence as your spellcasting ability for spells gained through your Archive.

entries.name: The Living Chronicle
entries: The Archive continuously and automatically records anything you personally see. Its entries are written as detailed narrative records resembling an exceptionally thorough novel or historical chronicle.

It can record locations, apparent time and sequence, people and creatures, appearance, clothing and equipment, expressions, gestures, visible actions, objects and surroundings, architecture and terrain, visible injuries, visible writing, environmental changes, and small visual details you genuinely witnessed.

It records only what you actually perceived. It doesn't invent unperceived information or automatically reveal invisible creatures, hidden motives, the truth behind disguises, or illusions you failed to recognize.

entries.name: Chronicle of the Keeper
entries: The Archive organizes your experiences into a continuous narrative and can arrange them by chapter, date, location, individual, subject, event, investigation, or other useful categories. Automatic Chronicle entries don't invent your private thoughts, emotions, assumptions, or conclusions unless you deliberately add them.

entries.name: Portrait Archive
entries: The Archive maintains detailed sketch-like portraits for every person you have personally known or encountered, preserving observable features such as face, hair, eyes, apparent age, distinctive traits, clothing, scars, markings, jewelry, and equipment.

entries.name: Familiar Faces
entries: When the Archive first becomes yours, it creates portraits for people you encountered before gaining this subclass using only details you genuinely remember. It can't fabricate forgotten or unknown details.

entries.name: Updating Portraits
entries: When you witness a person in a different appearance, the Archive can append a new portrait without replacing older ones. It doesn't automatically know radically different identities are the same creature unless you know that fact.

entries.name: Living Index
entries: The Archive maintains an automatically updating index. While holding it, you can take a Bonus Action to mentally request recorded information, causing it to open to or assemble the relevant entries. You can search by name, face, location, date, creature, object, spell, symbol, phrase, event, visual detail, or combinations of such information.

entries.name: Perfect Record
entries: Information automatically recorded by the Archive doesn't fade when your own memory does. Reading an entry can remind you of what was recorded but doesn't magically restore memories removed from your mind.

entries.name: The Archive Remembers
entries: Information accepted into the Archive can't be permanently lost through ordinary damage. Torn, burned, erased, soaked, stained, defaced, removed, or otherwise damaged recorded content restores itself the next time the Archive is opened. You can intentionally revise or erase notes you manually created, but automatic Chronicle records remain preserved unless a feature explicitly destroys them.

entries.name: Reconstitute the Archive
entries: If your Archive is lost or destroyed, you can perform a 1-hour ritual to recreate it. The recreated Archive contains all Wizard spells, Pact magic, Chronicle entries, portraits, maps, illustrations, research, manually archived information, and its Living Index. If the previous copy still exists, it disappears when the ritual is completed.

subclassFeature.name: Forbidden Invocations
entries: The Archive contains eldritch formulae stripped of the bargains and patrons through which they were originally discovered.

You gain two Eldritch Invocations of your choice from the Warlock class. You ignore all prerequisites for Eldritch Invocations gained through this feature, including Warlock level, character level, Pact, Patron or subclass, spell or cantrip, Warlock feature, another invocation, or any other listed prerequisite.

entries.name: Archived Substitution
entries: If an invocation refers to a prerequisite you don't possess, you are treated as possessing that prerequisite only for the purpose of using that invocation. This doesn't actually grant the prerequisite or qualify you for anything else.
If an invocation uses a spellcasting ability, spell attack modifier, or spell save DC, you can use your Intelligence and Wizard spellcasting statistics.
Whenever you gain a Wizard level, you can replace one invocation gained through this feature with another Eldritch Invocation, again ignoring its prerequisites.
Pact of the Tome granted by The Archive doesn't count toward this number.

subclassFeature.name: Archive Spells
entries: Certain formulae reveal themselves within the Archive as your ability to understand magic grows. When you reach a Wizard level shown in the Archive Spells table, the listed spells are automatically added to your Archive if they aren't already recorded there. Adding them requires no gold, time, or material expenditure. They aren't automatically prepared unless another feature says otherwise.

subclassFeature.name: Tome Convergence
entries: The Archive has no need to destroy knowledge in order to claim it. When another spellbook is brought against its pages, the two volumes overlap until their bindings, ink, and enchantments answer as one. For as long as they remain joined, the other tome becomes part of the Book of Shadows itself. When they separate, its enchantment departs with it, but the knowledge it carried remains behind.

entries.name: Merge Spellbook
entries: While touching your Archive and an eligible spellbook, you can perform a 10-minute ritual to merge the two. An eligible book is a spellbook, magical spellbook, grimoire, codex, tome, or similar written object that contains spells or magical research.

While merged, the other spellbook is physically incorporated into the Archive, is considered part of your Archive, and is treated as your Book of Shadows and your Wizard spellbook for the purpose of your features, spells, Eldritch Invocations, and other effects that refer to either.

You can use the merged spellbook's magical properties and abilities through the Archive. If one of its properties refers to "this book," "this spellbook," "this grimoire," or the item's own name, that reference can refer to the merged Archive for the duration of the merge.
Its Charges, limitations, activation requirements, Attunement, and other rules continue to apply normally. A merged spellbook remains the same magic item for those purposes.
You can have more than one eligible spellbook merged at the same time. Each remains a separate magic item for its Charges, Attunement, and item-specific rules.

entries.name: Attunement
entries: Merging a spellbook doesn't alter that item's Attunement. If you are already attuned to it, that Attunement continues normally while it is merged.

Merging doesn't create a second Attunement, transfer the Attunement to the Archive, or consume an additional Attunement slot. You can use the merged spellbook's Attunement-required properties through the Archive while that Attunement remains in effect.
If you weren't attuned to the spellbook before merging it, you can attune to it normally while it is merged. Separating the spellbook doesn't automatically end an existing Attunement to it.

entries.name: Perfect Copy
entries: When a spellbook merges with the Archive, the Archive automatically creates a complete copy of everything recorded within that book, including spells, rituals, formulae, notes, marginalia, drawings, diagrams, maps, research, instructions, illustrations, and other recorded information.
This copying requires no gold, special ink, or additional time. Wizard spells copied this way become permanently recorded in your Archive as though copied into your spellbook normally.

entries.name: Preserved Formulae
entries: If the merged spellbook contains a Wizard spell of a level too high for you to prepare or cast, the Archive can still preserve its written formula. You can't prepare or cast that spell until you would normally be able to do so as a Wizard.

entries.name: Separate Tome
entries: You can separate a merged spellbook from the Archive by performing a 1-minute ritual while touching the Archive. The original spellbook returns intact in your hand or in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you.

When separated, it ceases to be part of your Book of Shadows, and you lose access to its magic-item properties through the Archive. Its Charges, enchantments, and other magic-item properties remain with the original item.
The Archive permanently retains copies of its spells, writing, notes, diagrams, illustrations, and other recorded information.

entries.name: Independent Record
entries: After separation, the Archive's copy and the original book are independent. Changes made to one don't automatically alter the other. If the book is merged again later, the Archive copies any new or changed recorded information it doesn't already possess.

entries.name: Hovering Archive
entries: Beginning at 6th level, the Archive can hover and move through the air on its own. It can float beside you without being carried, follow you automatically, keep pace with your normal movement, remain nearby unless you direct it elsewhere, and move into your hand when you reach for it. These movements require no action from you.

subclassFeature.name: Open the Index
entries: Most wizards prepare only the handful of formulae their minds can safely hold at once. You no longer rely upon memory alone; the Archive searches itself faster than thought, exposing spell after spell in a torrent of perfect reference. For a brief interval, preparation ceases to be a limitation and the entirety of your collected spellcraft lies open before you.

As a Bonus Action, you can fully open the Archive's Living Index for 1 minute. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest, unless you expend a 4th-level or higher spell slot to activate it again.

entries.name: Every Page at Hand
entries: While Open the Index is active, every Wizard spell recorded in your Archive is treated as prepared. These spells don't count against the number of Wizard spells you can prepare. You still expend spell slots normally.

entries.name: Instant Reference
entries: The Archive automatically presents the necessary formula as part of a spell's casting.

entries.name: Assimilated Formulae
entries: Wizard spells copied through Tome Convergence qualify for Every Page at Hand normally.

entries.name: Perfect Recall
entries: While Open the Index is active, when you make an Intelligence ability check concerning a creature, location, object, symbol, event, spell, or other subject previously recorded by the Archive, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

entries.name: Consult the Archive
entries: While Open the Index is active, you can take a Bonus Action to request information contained within the Archive. It immediately presents all relevant passages, portraits, diagrams, observations, and cross-references it possesses. It can't reveal information it never recorded.

entries.name: Knowledge Overload
entries: Opening every path through the Archive at once forces impossible quantities of information through your mind.

Whenever you cast a Wizard spell that wasn't prepared before you activated Open the Index, you take Psychic damage immediately after casting it equal to {@damage 1d4} for each level of the spell. Cantrips cause no damage.
If this damage reduces you to 0 Hit Points, Open the Index immediately ends.

subclassFeature.name: The Archive Awakens
entries: For years, the Archive has watched, written, merged, and remembered. Eventually, countless fragments of knowledge cease behaving like a mere collection and begin moving with a single purpose. Pages turn before they are requested. Words appear before questions are finished. The book no longer waits patiently for its Keeper's hands.

entries.name: Beyond Attunement
entries: While a magic spellbook is merged with your Archive, the Archive can satisfy that spellbook's Attunement requirement on your behalf.
You can use the merged spellbook's properties as though you were attuned to it without attuning to the spellbook yourself, and doing so doesn't occupy one of your Attunement slots.

If you are already attuned to the merged spellbook, you can end that Attunement normally. You continue to gain access to its Attunement-required properties for as long as it remains merged with the Archive.
This feature doesn't remove or alter the spellbook's Attunement requirement for any other creature, nor does it transfer the item's Attunement to the Archive.
When the spellbook is separated from the Archive, this benefit immediately ends. You must be normally attuned to that spellbook to use any of its properties that require Attunement.
The Archive never permanently copies a merged spellbook's magical properties.

entries.name: Living Archive
entries: The Archive is now genuinely alive in a magical sense. It can independently open and close itself, turn and rearrange its pages, write and illustrate, present information it believes is relevant, move through the air, follow you, move itself away from obvious danger, and return to your hand when requested. Its ordinary movement and harmless behavior require no action from you.

entries.name: Voice of the Archive
entries: The Archive can communicate directly with you through written words, moving illustrations, audible speech, or direct mental communication. You and the Archive can communicate telepathically while within 1 mile of each other.
It understands languages you understand and can interpret languages sufficiently preserved within its pages, though this doesn't automatically teach those languages to you.

entries.name: Second Mind
entries: When you cast a Wizard spell that requires Concentration, you can have the Archive maintain Concentration on that spell instead of you. No action is required to assign the spell to the Archive.
While the Archive maintains Concentration, you can concentrate on another spell normally, and the Archive can maintain only one spell at a time.

The Archive never makes Constitution saving throws to maintain Concentration. Damage doesn't threaten its Concentration, effects that would normally force a Concentration saving throw don't affect its Concentration, and you becoming {@condition Incapacitated} doesn't end the Archive's Concentration.

The Archive's Concentration ends only if you die, the Archive is destroyed, you and the Archive become more than 1 mile apart, you choose to end the spell, the spell ends normally, or the Archive begins concentrating on another spell.

entries.name: Keeper and Archive
entries: While you and the Archive are on the same plane of existence, you always know its direction and approximate distance from you. If it is within 30 feet, you can cause it to immediately fly into your empty hand without using an action. The Archive always recognizes you as its Keeper regardless of changes to your appearance, age, disguise, transformation, physical form, or body.

subclassFeature.name: This Is Only the Beginning
entries: "Ninth-level magic? Is that truly where you believe magic ends?"
The Archive turns its own pages, almost amused by the thought that mortals could number infinity and declare the ninth circle its conclusion.
"You mistake the limits of those who came before you for the limits of magic itself."
"An Antimagic Field? You truly believe something so crude could stop me?"
The pages continue to turn even where magic itself is supposed to fall silent.
"No, Keeper. The ninth circle was never the end."
"It was merely the point where everyone else stopped."
"For us... this is only the beginning."

entries.name: Magic Without Permission
entries: Antimagic and similar effects can't suppress, nullify, disable, or prevent the functioning of your Wizard spells, your Wizard class features, your Archive subclass features, the Archive itself, magical properties of spellbooks currently merged through Tome Convergence, or spells maintained through Second Mind.
This includes {@spell Antimagic Field|XPHB}, dead-magic zones, magical nullification, and similar effects whose primary purpose is preventing or suppressing magic.
You can cast Wizard spells inside such an area, and your Wizard spells can enter, originate within, pass through, and continue functioning within it.
If you create an antimagic or magic-suppressing effect, you can choose for your own magic and the Archive to remain unaffected while it suppresses other magic normally.
This doesn't make you immune to hostile spells or magical effects merely because they are magical.

entries.name: Beyond the Ninth
entries: Once per Long Rest, you can cast one 9th-level Wizard spell recorded in your Archive without expending a spell slot. You cast it normally in all other respects, including casting time, components, material costs, and consumed components.

entries.name: Unshackled Formula
entries: When you cast a Wizard spell of 6th level or higher, a spell or magical effect of a lower level than the spell you cast can't counter, dispel, suppress, or end that spell solely by suppressing magic. Effects of the same or a higher level can still interact with it normally unless another feature says otherwise.

entries.name: No Final Page
entries: If a rule or effect treats 9th level as the maximum spell level, that restriction doesn't prevent a feature of The Archive from enhancing, reproducing, protecting, modifying, or otherwise interacting with your 9th-level spells.
This feature doesn't create 10th-level spells or 10th-level spell slots. Ninth level was never the limit of magic; it was merely the last limit you were taught.

subclassFeature.name: The Last Archivist
entries: There was once a difference between the Keeper and the Archive. One possessed the mind, while the other possessed the pages. After everything you have witnessed, preserved, and understood, that distinction has finally disappeared. The Archive no longer teaches you its knowledge. You simply remember what has always been written.

entries.name: The Archive Within
entries: Every Wizard spell recorded in your Archive is always prepared for you. These spells don't count against the number of Wizard spells you can prepare. You can cast them using your Wizard spell slots normally even if the physical Archive isn't currently in your possession.

entries.name: Perfect Index
entries: You no longer need to activate Open the Index to gain Every Page at Hand. That benefit is permanently active.

entries.name: Knowledge Mastered
entries: Knowledge Overload no longer affects you.

entries.name: No Knowledge Lost
entries: Anything permanently contained within the Archive remains available through your supernatural bond with it. If the Archive is lost, sealed, suppressed, or destroyed, you retain access to its recorded Wizard spells and your Archive subclass features.

entries.name: The Final Keeper
entries: The Archive can no longer be permanently separated from you. If it is destroyed, you can use a Bonus Action to recreate it in an empty hand or an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you.

The recreated Archive retains every recorded spell, Chronicle entry, portrait, illustration, map, formula, and other preserved record. Tome Convergence doesn't duplicate an external magic item; a merged spellbook remains the same original item.
Once you recreate the Archive this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: There Is No Final Page
entries: Whenever an Archive feature requires a spell, formula, or piece of information to exist within the Archive, you can access it regardless of the physical book's location. The Archive may still possess endless pages. You simply no longer need to turn them.

spell.name: Private Audience

components.m: a folded scrap of paper bearing two written names

entries: A soft boundary settles around the conversation, turning ordinary words into something meant only for those invited to hear them.
Voices remain natural to the speakers, yet beyond the boundary they lose shape and meaning.
A watcher may see mouths move and expressions change, but the conversation itself refuses to travel where it wasn't invited.
The spell doesn't erase the gathering from sight; it simply grants the speakers a room made from privacy rather than walls.

entries.name: Private Conversation
entries: Choose a point you can see within range. For the duration, a 10-foot-radius sphere centered on that point muffles deliberate conversation among creatures inside it.

When you cast the spell, you can designate any number of creatures you can see. A designated creature can hear and understand speech originating inside the sphere normally. Other creatures outside the sphere hear only indistinct murmuring and can't discern the words by reading lips.

Ordinary recording devices and unattended magical sensors outside the sphere likewise record only indistinct murmuring from speech originating inside it. This spell doesn't conceal creatures, block other sounds, or prevent a creature from entering the area.
As a Bonus Action while you are inside the sphere, you can move its center to a point you can see within 30 feet of you.

spell.name: Borrowed Mastery
entries: Every practiced motion leaves a pattern in the mind long after conscious thought has stopped guiding it.
You touch that pattern in another creature and borrow the shape of its experience.
For a short time, unfamiliar movements arrive with the confidence of long repetition.
The knowledge is borrowed rather than stolen; its owner loses nothing when you make use of it.

entries.name: Borrowed Proficiency
entries: Touch one willing creature and choose one skill, tool, weapon, or language proficiency it has. You gain the chosen proficiency for the duration. The target retains the proficiency.
If the chosen proficiency is a skill or tool in which you are already proficient, you instead add {@dice 1d4} to ability checks you make using that proficiency for the duration.
This spell doesn't grant Expertise, class features, weapon properties, or supernatural abilities associated with the chosen proficiency.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of level 2 or higher, you can borrow one additional proficiency from the same target for each slot level above 1.

spell.name: Arcane Familiarity

components.m: a short length of thread tied around a written word

entries: Understanding doesn't always require mastery; sometimes the mind only needs a temporary path through unfamiliar knowledge.
You trace such a path into a willing creature, giving strange symbols, tools, or practiced tasks the texture of something already known.
The spell doesn't replace experience, but it makes the unfamiliar feel close enough to use.
For several hours, the borrowed familiarity sits at the edge of instinct and disappears as quietly as it arrived.

entries.name: Familiar Knowledge
entries: Touch one willing creature and choose one skill proficiency, tool proficiency, or language. The target gains that proficiency for the duration.

If the target is already proficient in the chosen skill or tool, it instead adds {@dice 1d4} to ability checks it makes using that proficiency for the duration. If it already knows the chosen language, choose a different option.

spell.name: Arcane Poise
entries: You smooth the visible edges of uncertainty without replacing the creature's thoughts or personality.
Breathing steadies, hesitation becomes easier to hide, and words arrive without the small betrayals of nervousness.
The spell doesn't make a lie true or an argument persuasive by itself.
It simply gives the target the composure to present itself as though the moment were entirely under control.

entries.name: Composed Bearing
entries: Touch one willing creature. For the duration, whenever the target makes a Charisma ability check and rolls a 7 or lower on the d20, it can treat the d20 roll as an 8.
The target also has Advantage on ability checks made specifically to maintain composure, conceal nervousness, or speak convincingly under pressure.

spell.name: Perfect Recollection
entries: Memory is usually an act of reconstruction, colored by expectation and worn down by repetition.
This spell briefly replaces reconstruction with retrieval.
Details you genuinely perceived return in their original arrangement: wording, sequence, position, color, and sound.
Nothing new is revealed, but what was once noticed can be examined again with impossible clarity.

entries.name: Exact Recall
entries: For the duration, you can perfectly recall sensory details that you personally perceived during the previous 24 hours. You can reproduce remembered wording, images, sounds, sequences, and positions with the accuracy of your original perception.
You have Advantage on Intelligence checks made solely to recall or analyze those remembered details.
The spell doesn't reveal information you never perceived, correct a false perception, recover a memory that was magically removed, or identify something you failed to recognize at the time.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The period of memory you can access increases to 7 days with a 2nd-level slot, 30 days with a 3rd-level slot, 1 year with a 4th-level slot, and any memory you still possess with a 5th-level or higher slot.

spell.name: Arcane Edge

components.m: an iron filing wrapped in parchment

entries: A thin mathematical shimmer settles along a weapon's striking surface.
Its balance changes by fractions too small to see, aligning every blow with a sharpened magical vector.
The weapon doesn't become heavier or visibly larger, yet each successful strike carries a second edge made from force.
For a few minutes, technique and spellcraft occupy the same line.

entries.name: Spell-Sharpened Weapon
entries: Touch one weapon. For the duration, the weapon is magical, and attacks made with it can use your spellcasting ability modifier instead of Strength or Dexterity for the attack and damage rolls.
On a hit, the weapon deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Force damage.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The extra Force damage increases by {@damage 1d6} for each slot level above 1.

spell.name: Mystic Aegis

time.condition: which you take when you or a creature you can see within 30 feet is hit by an attack or fails a saving throw

entries: A defense need not be a wall; sometimes the smallest correction is enough to turn catastrophe aside.
You cast a brief lattice of force around a creature at the instant danger finds it.
The lattice tightens around the threat already in motion, then remains as a faint protective geometry for a few heartbeats.
Its purpose is not to make the target untouchable, but to give it one more chance to endure.

entries.name: Reactive Aegis
entries: Choose the triggering creature. If the trigger was an attack, the target gains a +3 bonus to AC against that attack, potentially causing it to miss. If the trigger was a failed saving throw, the target adds {@dice 1d4} to that saving throw, potentially turning it into a success.
Until the start of the target's next turn, it also gains a +1 bonus to AC and saving throws.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When cast with a slot of level 2 or higher, the lingering bonus to AC and saving throws increases by 1 for every two slot levels above 1, to a maximum of +4.

spell.name: Vortex
entries: You pinch space into a brief rotational collapse around a creature.
Dust, loose cloth, and nearby debris twist inward before the distortion snaps shut.
The pull is violent but fleeting, dragging the target toward the center of the impossible spiral.
What remains afterward is only displaced air and the memory of motion.

entries.name: Collapsing Spiral
entries: Choose one creature you can see within range. It must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 2d10} Force damage and is pulled up to 15 feet toward a point you choose within 5 feet of it. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn't pulled.
A creature can choose to fail the saving throw.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@damage 1d10} for each slot level above 1.

spell.name: Shared Concentration
entries: Concentration is usually a private burden, a single mind holding a spell's structure against interruption.
You expose that structure for a heartbeat and place it into another willing mind.
The spell itself doesn't change hands; only the responsibility for keeping it intact does.
Once the transfer is complete, your thoughts are free while another creature carries the unbroken formula.

entries.name: Transfer Concentration
entries: Choose one willing creature you can see within range. If you are concentrating on a spell, you can transfer Concentration on that spell to the target.

The spell retains its original spellcasting ability, spell save DC, spell attack modifier, targets, choices, remaining duration, and all other statistics. The target doesn't need to know or be able to cast the spell.

The target now follows the normal rules for maintaining Concentration on that spell, and your Concentration on it ends without ending the spell. You can immediately concentrate on another spell normally.

spell.name: Arcane Reversal

time.condition: which you take when you succeed on a saving throw against a spell that targets only you, or when a spell attack misses you

entries: A spell that fails to seize you still possesses momentum, intent, and a path through the world.
Rather than allowing that structure to collapse, you catch it at the instant of failure.
With a sharp redirection, the hostile formula leaves its original path and seeks a new legal target.
You don't recast the magic; you merely refuse to let its missed opportunity go to waste.

entries.name: Redirect Spell
entries: Choose another creature you can see that would be a valid target for the triggering spell if the spell originated from your space. The triggering spell is redirected to that creature.

The original caster's spellcasting ability, spell save DC, spell attack modifier, spell level, and other statistics are unchanged. The spell isn't cast again, and no additional spell slot or components are used.
This spell can't redirect a spell that targets more than one creature, creates an area of effect, targets an object, or has a range of Self.

spell.name: Arcane Backlash
entries: You lace a creature's spellcasting with a hostile resonance that waits for magical structure to pass through it.
The mark is quiet until the victim reaches for a spell.
Then the resonance turns the act of casting against its source, striking through the same mental channels needed to sustain magic.
The more powerful the attempted spell, the more violently the backlash answers.

entries.name: Backlash Mark
entries: Choose one creature you can see within range. It must make an Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, it is marked for the duration.
Whenever the marked creature casts a spell of level 1 or higher, it takes {@damage 1d8} Force damage plus Force damage equal to twice the level of the spell it cast.
If this damage causes the creature to make a saving throw to maintain Concentration, it has Disadvantage on that saving throw.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The Force damage increases by {@damage 1d8} for each slot level above 2.

spell.name: Borrowed Moment

time.condition: which you take when a creature you can see within 60 feet starts its turn

entries: A turn is only a small allotment of possibility, but possibility can be stolen.
You hook one piece of an unfolding moment and pull it away before the creature can spend it.
The stolen fragment arrives in your own future as motion, speed, or an opening to act.
For an instant, initiative stops being an order and becomes something negotiable.

entries.name: Steal a Moment
entries: The triggering creature must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, choose one of the following resources: its Action, its Bonus Action, or an amount of its movement equal to its Speed.

The creature loses the chosen resource for the current turn. Before the end of your next turn, you gain the corresponding resource once: one additional Action, one additional Bonus Action, or additional movement equal to the amount stolen.
An Action gained from this spell can be used normally, including to cast a spell of level 1 or higher. Any unused stolen resource disappears at the end of your next turn.

spell.name: Deferred Wound

time.condition: which you take when a creature you can see within 30 feet takes damage

entries: You don't heal the wound; you refuse to allow the injury to finish happening yet.
For a few seconds, cuts remain unopened, burns hold their heat without consuming flesh, and impacts wait outside the body.
Every new injury joins the same suspended account.
When the delay ends, the body must finally pay everything that time was forced to hold.

entries.name: Deferred Damage
entries: Choose the creature that took the triggering damage. Reduce that triggering damage to 0 and record the amount and damage type that was prevented.
Until the end of the target's next turn, whenever it would take damage, reduce that damage to 0 and record the prevented amount and its damage type.
At the end of the target's next turn, it takes all recorded damage at once, preserving the original damage types and amounts. Healing received before that moment doesn't reduce the recorded damage.
Resistance, Immunity, Vulnerability, and other damage modifications are applied when each instance of damage is originally deferred and aren't applied a second time when the recorded damage is taken.

spell.name: Gravity Tilt
entries: You don't increase gravity; you persuade it that a different direction is down.
The target's balance becomes meaningless as the world seems to rotate without moving.
Walls become floors, open air becomes a fall, and every loose object suddenly agrees with the new orientation.
The effect persists only while your spell holds the false direction in place.

entries.name: Personal Down
entries: Choose one creature you can see within range and one direction. The creature must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, that direction becomes down for the target for the duration.

At the start of each of the target's turns, it falls up to 20 feet in that direction unless something stops the fall. A collision can cause falling damage as normal, treating the distance traveled before the collision as the fall distance.
At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the saving throw, ending the spell on itself on a success.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The maximum distance the target falls at the start of each turn increases by 10 feet for each slot level above 2.

spell.name: Forgotten Presence

components.m: ash from a burned name or portrait

entries: A person leaves traces everywhere: a remembered face, a written name, an image, a pattern of references that says they were here.
You loosen those traces without removing the person who created them.
At first the world merely becomes uncertain; stronger castings can make records and recollections fail together.
The spell doesn't rewrite history. It makes the evidence of identity increasingly difficult for the world to hold.

entries.name: Fading Identity
entries: Touch one willing creature. For the duration, creatures other than you have Disadvantage on ability checks made solely to remember, identify, or connect the target to a past encounter unless they are currently observing the target.
Ordinary notes, labels, and records that identify the target remain present, but a creature searching them has Disadvantage on ability checks made to locate or connect those records to the target.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The spell gains the following cumulative effects when cast with higher-level slots:

items: {@b 3rd Level.} Casual memories of the target's name and appearance become vague unless deliberately refreshed by observing the target or an identifying record.

{@b 4th Level.} Ordinary written references, portraits, photographs, and similar identifying records become blurred, incomplete, or contextless for the duration; the underlying objects aren't destroyed.
{@b 5th Level.} Ordinary recordings and stored identifying data are affected in the same way, and creatures can't gain Advantage on checks to identify the target from such evidence.
{@b 6th Level.} Divination spells of 5th level or lower that are used solely to identify or locate the target from its identity fail to gain useful identifying information.
{@b 7th Level.} Memories that directly identify the target become inaccessible while the spell lasts, though a creature still remembers the events themselves with the target's identity indistinct.
{@b 8th Level.} Magical and ordinary identifying records of the target are suppressed for the duration unless protected by an Artifact, deity, or magic of comparable power.
{@b 9th Level.} All preceding effects apply, and the spell lasts Until Dispelled.

spell.name: Trait Exchange
entries: Bodies solve problems in different ways: fins answer water, wings answer distance, claws answer stone, and unfamiliar senses answer darkness.
You draw one such physical solution from a willing body and rewrite it into another.
The change is visible, producing whatever temporary anatomy is necessary for the borrowed capability.
Nothing is created from theory alone; one creature must surrender the trait while another carries it.

entries.name: Exchange Physical Capability
entries: Choose two willing creatures you can see within range. Choose one eligible physical capability possessed by one creature, the donor. The donor loses that capability for the duration, and the other creature, the recipient, gains it.

Eligible capabilities include a Climb, Swim, Burrow, or Fly Speed; Darkvision; Blindsight out to no more than 30 feet; the ability to breathe underwater or in a specific natural environment; a natural adaptation that lets the donor survive ordinary extreme heat or cold; a natural weapon; or a natural body feature used for movement.

The recipient develops temporary anatomy appropriate to the borrowed trait. If the trait is a natural weapon, the recipient uses its own Strength or Dexterity, as appropriate, for the attack and damage rolls and uses the weapon's original damage die, damage type, reach, and physical form. Special riders aren't transferred unless they are inseparable from the physical structure of the weapon.
Either participant can take a Bonus Action to end the exchange for itself, returning the trait to the donor and ending that transferred capability.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: You can transfer one additional eligible capability between the same two creatures for each slot level above 2.

spell.name: Borrowed Shelter
entries: You weave protection as a set of interchangeable answers rather than a single shield.
The pattern can harden against weapons, brace the body, steady the mind, or fold distance into cover.
Because the shelter is borrowed from possibility rather than fixed form, you can reweave it as danger changes.
The spell's strength lies in being the right defense a heartbeat before it is needed.

entries.name: Choose a Shelter
entries: Choose one willing creature you can see within range and choose one of the following shelters:

items: {@b Bulwark.} The target gains a +2 bonus to AC.
{@b Endurance.} Choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Radiant, or Thunder. The target gains Resistance to the chosen damage type.
{@b Steady Mind.} The target has Advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws.
{@b Sure Body.} The target has Advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saving throws.
{@b Covering Veil.} The target has Half Cover against ranged attacks and effects that originate more than 10 feet away from it.

entries.name: Reweave
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can change the shelter affecting one target of the spell to another option.

entries.name: Emergency Shift
entries: When a target of the spell is hit by an attack or fails a saving throw, you can take a Reaction to change that target's shelter before the triggering attack or saving throw is resolved. The new shelter applies to the triggering event if relevant.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: You can target one additional willing creature for each slot level above 2. Each target can have a different shelter. Reweave and Emergency Shift affect only one target at a time.

spell.name: Spell Graft
entries: You treat a spell as a transferable structure rather than a private piece of training.
The formula takes root in another willing mind, carrying with it just enough understanding to be used.
For a while, the recipient can reach for magic it may never have studied and may not normally be able to learn.
The graft is temporary, but while it lasts the borrowed formula behaves as though it belongs there.

entries.name: Graft a Spell
entries: Touch one willing creature and choose one cantrip or level 1 spell that you know or have prepared. The target knows that spell for the duration, even if it has no Spellcasting feature or the spell isn't on any of its spell lists.
The target uses your spellcasting ability, spell attack modifier, and spell save DC for the grafted spell and follows the spell's normal casting rules and components.

The target can cast the grafted spell once without expending a spell slot. A free casting waives Material components that have no listed cost, but Material components with a listed cost are still required and are consumed normally if the spell says so.

After the free casting is used, the target can cast a grafted spell of level 1 or higher only by expending one of its own spell slots of an appropriate level. A grafted cantrip can be cast any number of times while the spell lasts.

You retain the chosen spell. You can maintain only one Spell Graft at a time. Either you or the target can end the graft at any time without using an action; casting this spell again also ends your previous graft.

items: {@b 2nd Level.} Cantrip or level 1 spell; duration 1 hour.
{@b 3rd Level.} Spell of level 2 or lower; duration 4 hours.
{@b 4th Level.} Spell of level 3 or lower; duration 8 hours.
{@b 5th Level.} Spell of level 4 or lower; duration 24 hours.
{@b 6th Level.} Spell of level 5 or lower; duration 3 days.
{@b 7th Level.} Spell of level 6 or lower; duration 7 days.
{@b 8th Level.} Spell of level 7 or lower; duration 30 days.
{@b 9th Level.} Spell of level 8 or lower; duration Until Dispelled.

spell.name: Affliction Relay
entries: An affliction is more than a condition; it is a relationship between an effect and the creature forced to bear it.
You seize that relationship and reroute it.
Blindness can jump from one set of eyes to another, fear can abandon its first victim, and restraints can reform as spectral equivalents around a new body.
The spell doesn't imitate an affliction. It moves, inherits, or severs the original burden.

entries.name: Choose an Affliction
entries: Choose one creature you can see within range that is affected by one instance of the Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Frightened, Grappled, Poisoned, or Restrained condition. Choose one of the following options.

entries.name: Transfer
entries: Choose a second creature within 30 feet of the first creature. The second creature must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the chosen condition ends on the original creature and affects the second creature instead.

The transferred condition retains its original source, remaining duration, saving throw DC, repeat-save timing, ending conditions, and other rules. If the original condition depended on a physical connection that can't literally move, an equivalent spectral restraint or connection manifests for the transferred condition.

entries.name: Take
entries: You can choose yourself as the second creature. If you do, no saving throw is required; the chosen condition ends on the original creature and affects you instead.

entries.name: Sever
entries: Instead of transferring the condition, make an ability check using your spellcasting ability. The DC equals 10 + the level of the spell or magical effect causing the condition. If the effect has no level, the GM assigns it a level from 1 to 9 based on its power. On a success, the chosen condition ends.

entries.name: Borrowed Origin
entries: A transferred affliction remains the same effect for the purpose of immunity, suppression, removal, and interactions with its original source.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When cast with a 3rd-level slot, you can also relay the Incapacitated condition; with a 4th-level slot, Paralyzed; with a 5th-level slot, Stunned; and with a 6th-level or higher slot, Petrified.

spell.name: Mirror Wound

time.condition: which you take when a creature you can see within 60 feet takes damage

entries: Pain creates a shape in the instant it enters a body.
You catch that shape before it settles and reflect part of it into another living vessel.
With consent, the burden can be divided precisely; without it, the second body can resist becoming the mirror.
The wound remains real throughout. Only its ownership changes.

entries.name: Mirror the Damage
entries: Choose the creature that took the triggering damage and one other creature you can see within range.

entries.name: Share
entries: If both creatures are willing, divide the triggering damage between them in any proportion. The total amount and the original damage types remain unchanged.

entries.name: Take
entries: If you are the second creature, you can take any amount of the triggering damage without making a saving throw, reducing the original creature's damage by the same amount.

entries.name: Reflect
entries: If the second creature is unwilling, it must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, you can transfer up to half the triggering damage, rounded up, from the original creature to the second creature. On a successful save, no damage is transferred.

entries.name: Separate Defenses
entries: Resistance, Immunity, and Vulnerability apply separately to each creature when that creature takes its portion of the damage.

entries.name: No Recursion
entries: Damage created or transferred by Mirror Wound can't trigger another casting of Mirror Wound.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell with a slot of level 3 or higher, the maximum amount you can transfer using Reflect increases by 10 damage for each slot level above 2 and can exceed half the triggering damage.
When cast with a 5th-level or higher slot, you can divide transferred damage among up to two secondary creatures. Each unwilling secondary creature makes its own Constitution saving throw.

spell.name: Sealed Agreement

components.m: a written agreement bearing the mark or signature of every participant

entries: A promise becomes dangerous when magic is allowed to remember its exact wording.
You bind a voluntary agreement into a seal that watches only the clauses its participants knowingly accept.
The spell doesn't compel anyone to sign or force obedience in advance.
Instead, it ensures that a deliberate breach has a consequence none of the participants can pretend they never accepted.

entries.name: Participants and Terms
entries: Choose any number of willing creatures within range that can understand the agreement. Every participant must knowingly and willingly accept the same written terms throughout the casting. If any participant withdraws consent before the casting ends, that creature isn't bound.

The agreement can contain any number of ordinary clauses, but you designate up to three of them as Sealed Clauses. A creature breaches a Sealed Clause only when it knowingly performs an act that clearly violates that clause. Ambiguous, impossible, or involuntary conduct doesn't count as a breach.

entries.name: Breach Consequence
entries: For each Sealed Clause, choose one of the following consequences when you cast the spell. When a bound creature knowingly breaches that clause, the chosen consequence affects that creature for the remaining duration of the agreement unless the consequence says otherwise:

items: {@b Sealed Movement.} All of the breaching creature's Speeds are halved.

{@b Restless Torment.} Whenever the breaching creature attempts to finish a Short Rest or Long Rest, it must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, magical torment prevents it from gaining any benefits from that rest. It makes this saving throw separately for each rest it attempts.

{@b Withering Judgment.} When the creature breaches the clause, and again at each dawn while this consequence remains, it takes {@damage 6d10} Necrotic damage. This damage ignores Resistance and Immunity to Necrotic damage. Each time the creature takes this damage, its Hit Point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. This reduction lasts until this consequence ends.

{@b Arcane Retribution.} Choose Psychic or Force when you create the agreement. When the creature breaches the clause, it takes {@damage 8d6} damage of the chosen type. At each dawn while this consequence remains, the breaching creature and every creature within 10 feet of it take {@damage 2d6} damage of the chosen type.

{@b Arcane Vulnerability.} The breaching creature takes a penalty to saving throws against spells and magical effects. The penalty equals the level of the spell slot used to cast Sealed Agreement minus 1: -2 with a 3rd-level slot, -3 with a 4th-level slot, -4 with a 5th-level slot, -5 with a 6th-level slot, -6 with a 7th-level slot, -7 with an 8th-level slot, and -8 with a 9th-level slot.

entries.name: Spell Clause
entries: Instead of one normal breach consequence, you can designate a Spell Clause. Choose a spell of level 1 or lower that you know or have prepared, has a casting time of an Action or Bonus Action, and can target a single creature. If a participant breaches that clause, the chosen spell is cast on that participant at the next dawn as though you cast it using the same spellcasting ability used for Sealed Agreement. Any costly or consumed Material components required by the chosen spell must be provided during the casting of Sealed Agreement.
A participant can't be affected by more than one Spell Clause from the same Sealed Agreement at a single dawn.

entries.name: Ending the Agreement
entries: The agreement ends early for every participant if every currently bound participant willingly agrees to end it while within 30 feet of one another.

entries.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When cast with a 4th-level slot, the duration becomes 1 year. When cast with a 5th-level or higher slot, the duration becomes Until Dispelled.

spell.name: Permanency

m.text: special inks worth 1,000 GP, which the spell consumes

entries: Most spells are written with an ending built into their structure.
You spend an hour finding that final line and replacing it with a self-sustaining loop.
